options: Announce 'this happened' to any number of listeners it knows NOTHING about
explanation: Publisher and subscribers are decoupled: the timer knows nothing of loggers or UI, and listeners know nothing of each other. Observer (2.14), built in.

stem: Why 'event Action<int> Tick' instead of a public Action<int> field?
options: event restricts outsiders to += and -= ONLY - nobody can wipe others' subscriptions or fire it externally
explanation: With a plain field, any code could do timer.Tick = null or timer.Tick.Invoke(999). The event keyword reserves assign-and-raise for the declaring class.

options: An event with NO subscribers is null - bare Invoke would crash the publisher
explanation: One of the most common event bugs: everything works until the day nobody happens to be subscribed.

stem: timer.Tick -= s => Console.WriteLine(s); after adding the same-looking lambda removes:
options: NOTHING - it is a different lambda instance; -= needs the SAME reference you added
explanation: Store the delegate in a variable if you will ever detach it. An anonymous lambda added inline is gone beyond reach.

stem: A long-lived publisher with never-unsubscribed handlers causes:
options: A memory leak - the publisher's invocation list keeps every subscriber ALIVE
explanation: The delegate holds a reference to each subscriber object (4.8's managed leak). Long-running apps must -= what they +=.
EventHandler<TEventArgs>: sender says WHO raised it (useful when one handler watches many), e carries the data in an EventArgs subclass.

stem: Raising through 'protected virtual void OnItemAdded(BasketEventArgs e)' exists so that:
options: Subclasses can extend or intercept the raise
explanation: The protected virtual OnX method is the standard extension point - a derived Basket can add behaviour around the announcement.

options: Past tense: Clicked, Saved, ItemAdded - 'it happened'
explanation: The name announces a completed fact. (Pre-events like 'Closing' exist for cancellable operations.)

stem: In 7.3, Died fires only when health CROSSES zero, not on every hit at zero. Why guard inside the publisher?
options: So no subscriber ever needs to de-duplicate - the event means exactly one thing, once
explanation: Put the semantics in the publisher: 'Died' as a single fact beats every listener writing its own already-dead bookkeeping.

stem: One object calling ONE known collaborator and needing a result back should use:
options: A plain method call - events are broadcast and fire-and-forget
explanation: Events shine for optional, multiple, unknown listeners. A known single callee wanting a return value is just... a method.
